A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial presentation changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of three VL decoders, including benchmark scores, modality contributions, self-consistency tests, and individual examples in Tables 1–11.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the detailed tables, uncertainty plots, and case studies in its appendix.

M1.justification: The MM-SHAP normalization, averaging, and modality aggregation procedures remain unchanged, as do CC-SHAP and the six edit-based tests. Rewording and discussion of alternative aggregation strategies do not introduce a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate VQA, GQA, GQA balanced, MSCOCO, FoilIt, and the same VALSE instruments. Free-form generation, pairwise caption selection, and image-sentence alignment coverage are retained.

E2.justification: The decoder models, encoder/unimodal reference comparisons, and six edit-based comparison tests are retained. Table 1 removes the explicit Random row, but preserves the same 50% chance comparison in its caption.

E3.justification: Both versions use all VALSE samples for benchmarking and 100 random samples per dataset or instrument for the SHAP and self-consistency experiments. Models, metrics, prompts, answer-order randomization, and post-hoc/CoT settings are unchanged; prompts are relocated to Appendix A.2.

E4.justification: The linguistic-phenomenon analyses, explanation comparisons, and horse/bench case studies in Tables 4–11 are retained. Section 6.3 proposes investigating alternative aggregation strategies but reports no new ablation.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same three-run standard-deviation analyses for existence and VQA in Figures 7–8. The new Section 6.2 points to existing uncertainty evidence without changing its reporting practice or run counts.

E6.justification: Evaluated-model scores in Tables 1–3 and outcomes in Tables 4–11 are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains average pairwise accuracies of 85%, 83%, and 79% for LLaVA-NeXT-Mistral, BakLLaVA, and LLaVA-NeXT-Vicuna respectively; redesigned plots display the same results.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 retain the same mathematical definitions and operations; changes from p-based to N-based token-count notation are equivalent. The new discussion of averaging is a methodological qualification, not a new formal assumption, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and principal claims: text-heavy predictions, greater image contributions during explanations, lower VLM self-consistency than LLMs, and continuing difficulty on VALSE.

C2.justification: New Section 6 explicitly identifies the English-model and open-model evaluation scope, acknowledges that averaging has not been demonstrated superior to alternative aggregation, and discusses possible application to closed-source APIs. The existing compute discussion is mostly relocated from v1 Appendix A.1.

D1.justification: v1 provides a concrete code repository link, whereas v2 only promises future public availability. The reported GPU changes from NVIDIA A100 48 GB to A40 48 GB with unchanged timings; model links, prompts, FlashAttention-2, and quantization information are otherwise retained or relocated.

R1.justification: v2 adds Meister et al. (2022) and Garcia et al. (2023) in its ethics discussion and explicitly credits prior work for normalization in Section 3. The CC-SHAP reference's change from 2023b to its 2024 publication is an update to the same work.

P1.justification: The abstract and much of the main text are extensively tightened and rephrased. New Limitations and Ethics Statement sections reorganize the ending, while model links and prompts receive dedicated appendix subsections.

P2.justification: v1 Figure 3 becomes a redesigned front-page Figure 1, the MM-SHAP schematic is redrawn, and Figures 4–5 are substantially reformatted and integrated into the discussion. Table 2 moves to the appendix, and Table 1 replaces its chance row with caption information; these changes reorganize the display without adding experimental evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 improves attribution and explicitly acknowledges the unvalidated aggregation choice in Section 6.3. However, it replaces the concrete code link with an unspecified future release and compresses key plots, particularly Figure 4, reducing legibility. With empirical support unchanged, these opposing effects on clarity and reproducibility leave the net quality direction uncertain.
